chung.Syllabus Name: Mobility Applications Design 1 _Thiết kế ứng dụng cho các thiết bị di động 1
chung.Description: This course aimed to provide students knowledge related to Interaction and UX Design in mobility world including smartphone devices and other wearable ones. In this course, student will be taught the common principles which dominates on mobile interface design in general. Specified principles corresponding three popular mobile platforms such as Android, iOS and Windows are going to be discussed, too. An agile for researching and designing Interaction and UX in mobility will also be introduced and applied through out this course. At the end of this course, student will obtain practical experience via a three phase projects in which they have to apply learned principles. A high fidelity prototype tools and paper prototype techniques will be explained in this course.
chung.StudentTasks:
- Attend at least 80% of contact hours in order to be accepted to the final examination
- Follow instructions from teachers in class
- Actively participate in class activities
- Fulfill tasks given by instructor after class
- Read the textbook in advance
- Access the course website (https://flm.fpt.edu.vn) for up-to-date information and material of the course, for online supports from teachers and other students and for practicing and assessment.
- Complete course's Portfolio with full contents of exercises and submit to the teacher 1 day after the course

taiLieu: Don’t Make Me Think, Revisited - A Common Sense Approach to Web Usability
Helen Sharp , Jennifer Preece , Yvonne Rogers
Designed for Use: Create Usable Interfaces for Applications and the Web
Jenny Preece, Helen Sharp, Yvonne Rogers
Essential Mobile Interaction Design - Perfecting Interface Design in Mobile Apps
clo: Explain the core principles of interaction and user experience (UX) design in mobile and wearable contexts, including smartphones, smartwatches, and other responsive platforms.
Identify and analyze platform-specific UI/UX guidelines (e.g., Android, iOS, and others) and adapt design approaches accordingly.
Conduct UX and visual research to gather user needs, identify design patterns, and explore visual languages that inform concept development and design directions.
Apply the obtained knowledge to implement a research and designing process for a real product.

Investigate and analyze technologies relevant to the product context (e.g., APIs, sensors, databases), and propose practical solutions that define how data is processed and how user actions flow through the system.
Design and prototype digital products by expressing distinctive visual concepts through both low- and high-fidelity prototypes using up-to-date design tools and systems.
Evaluate user experience through usability testing and user feedback, and refine solutions through improvement cycles, focusing on consistency, performance, and emotional impact.
